senses.d: To become aware of, understand, or appreciate (a fact or situation, especially something which has been true for some time).
ex: He realized that he had left his umbrella on the train.
She desperately yelled at her young daughter, frantic to make her realize what she had done.

senses.d: To sense (something) strongly or vividly as if real.
To cause (something) to seem real; to make realistic; specifically, to present (something) clearly to the mind, a person, (archaic) oneself, etc., so that it seems real.
ex: Drawings appear fully realized in his mind's eye at a furious rate, before he even picks up his pencil.
Every action that realizes a dream or desire unrealizes it in reality.

senses.d: To convert (something imaginary or planned, as a goal or idea) into reality; to bring into real existence, to make real.
ex: Near-synonyms: implement, execute; actualize, materialize, embody; accomplish

senses.d: To achieve (one's) potential.
To convert (an asset or property, especially investments such as bonds, shares, etc.) into a more easily usable form such as money, especially by selling the asset or property.
ex: By realizing the company’s assets, the liquidator was able to return most of the shareholders’ investments.
Profits from the investment can be realized at any time by selling the shares.

senses.d: To acquire (money, a profit, etc.) by selling an asset or property, through trade, etc.; also (followed by on), to make (money or a profit) on an investment, a venture, etc.
ex: to realize large profits from a speculation

senses.d: Of an asset or property: to generate (a specific amount of money or interest) when invested or sold.
To turn (an abstract linguistic object, especially a phoneme) into a speech sound actually used in a language.
ex: The southern /v/ is realized as the voiced approximant [ʋ].

senses.d: To obtain an entity from (an abstract group or structure).
